first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses both the 4% decline in completion and the 6% activation decline, while prior evidence suggests durable self-serve adoption gains. I would verify the onboarding and signup experiments, and also check the promotional-pricing record to compare its qualified-revenue and downstream-quality tradeoffs before committing. A small guarded test limits risk to lead quality, retention, and monetization while preserving the option to scale.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding, directly targeting the 4% completion decline and 6% activation decline. The archived onboarding result showed completion up 13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention up 3%, making it the strongest sustainable-growth response. Signup simplification is supportive evidence for SMBs but carries a slight retention decline, so monitor qualified revenue and 30-day retention. Do not use promotional pricing: its 18% qualified-revenue lift was followed by a 12% retention decline and failed to survive renewal.
